snip.t: Gait assessment: Ataxic gait from proprioceptive loss; foot drop from peroneal weakness — Large‑fiber loss or motor weakness.
A 45‑year‑old woman with HIV on antiretroviral therapy develops symmetric distal numbness and foot drop over 2 months.
Mononeuritis multiplex (asymmetric sensory loss, foot drop): Segmental ischemia of peripheral nerves due to vasa nervorum involvement.
| What causes foot drop? | Weak dorsiflexion, commonly due to common fibular neuropathy or L5 radiculopathy |
snip.s: CNS Examination: Complete IMED Year 4 Notes

snip.t: Inability to Lift the Front Part of the Foot: Weakness in the muscles that lift the front part of the foot can result in foot drop, making it difficult to walk.

qs.q: Three weeks after accidental exposure to tri-cresyl phosphate, a patient develops a symmetrical distal sensorimotor neuropathy characterized by foot drop. What is the primary pathological mechanism?
o: Demyelination of central nervous system tracts
Primary loss of anterior horn cells in the spinal cord
Length‑dependent axonal degeneration of peripheral nerves
Direct destruction of skeletal muscle fibers
qs.e: OPIDP results from neuropathy target esterase inhibition, causing length-dependent dying-back axonal neuropathy.
